Fundamental, Excess, the Total Charge; Repulsive and Attractive Electric Forces

All protons and all electrons have the same magnitude of electric charge. This value is called the fundamental charge and is often designated as e =1.6 x 10-19C where C represents Coulombs which is the unit of charge. Protons are said to have positive charge and electrons have negative charge.

Let np be the number of protons at a point (or small region of space). Then the total positive charge (qtpc or just q) at that point is np times the fundamental charge or

q = npe.

If there were np protons and ne electrons is a small region of space, the total charge or net charge or excess charge would be

qnet = (np - ne)e.

The figures below show a collection of protons (left) and collection of protons and electrons (right).

Recall a mole of molecules is Avogadro's number (NA = 6.022x1023) of molecules. If the number of moles is nmoles and each molecule has np protons, then the total positive charge (TPC) is qtpc = nmolesNAnpe.

 

Repulsive and Attractive Forces

Two positive point charges near each other experience a repulsive electric force. Likewise, two negative charge near each other experience a repulsive electric force. A positive point charge and negative point charge near each other experience an attractive electric force. These forces are shown below.
